With the 2026 World Cup nearing its end, Major League Soccer (MLS) will return to Apple TV tomorrow, with a series of related features also launching simultaneously on Apple Maps, Apple Sports, Apple Fitness+, and other platforms. Details are as follows.

MLS Returns to Apple TV

Apple is highlighting the return of MLS today, with six matches scheduled over the coming days:

July 16 (Thursday):

  • CF Montréal vs Toronto FC (7:30 PM Eastern Time)
  • Chicago Fire vs Vancouver Whitecaps (8:30 PM Eastern Time)
  • St. Louis City SC vs Sporting Kansas City (8:30 PM Eastern Time)
  • Seattle Sounders FC vs Portland Timbers (10:30 PM Eastern Time)

July 17 (Friday):

  • Nashville SC vs Atlanta United FC (8:10 PM Eastern Time)
  • LA Galaxy vs LAFC (10:15 PM Eastern Time)

To celebrate the return of the regular season, Apple has announced a series of MLS-themed features across its platforms, including a brand-new "Time to Walk" audio experience for Apple Fitness+ subscribers.

The new episode features German football legend Thomas Müller, who "reflects on the effort he put in before his career took off, and shares how to face the challenges of major life transitions with composure."

Apple Music will also launch a number of exclusive playlists curated by the players themselves, including playlists by Diego Luna of Real Salt Lake and Evander da Silva Ferreira of FC Cincinnati, as well as themed playlists centered on multiple clubs from the Eastern and Western Conferences, such as the New York Red Bulls, New York City FC, and Orlando City SC.

On Apple Maps, Apple will launch "matchday guides produced by MLS clubs, as well as city tours curated by the players, to help users discover matchday restaurants, explore popular hotspots in the city, and gain a deeper understanding of each stadium."

Users who rely on the Apple Sports app can stay up to date with the latest league developments through live scores, standings, live text commentary, lineups, and team statistics.

Finally, Apple noted:

MLS matches are available for free to Apple TV subscribers in more than 100 countries and regions worldwide. Apple also offers exclusive content and viewing access to various cup competitions and the playoffs throughout the entire season.

To learn more about Apple's coverage of the MLS return, please click on this link.

Apple TV costs $12.99 per month, or it can be subscribed to through the Apple One bundle. The platform offers a number of popular series and films, including "Stick", "The Studio", "The Morning Show", "Disclaimer", and "Severance".
